races.name: Ladies Day At Dundalk Handicap

runners_data.name: Valiant Force
runners_data.note: Course specialist with strong Dundalk AW record but a confirmed hold-up runner who will need things to go wrong up front; Robson De Aguiar yard in modest 14-day form (1/12), and sim-going figures show a creditable 3W5P suggesting track suits, but the pace dynamic here does not set up well for a horse who needs a strong gallop to close into.
runners_data.comment: Tops our figures despite a modest recent sequence, unplaced last time and twice ninth before that in six starts without a win. Race fit after a 15-day break, with form over today's distance and going from draw 6, though the finishing figures give little encouragement lately.

runners_data.name: The Highway Rat
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old veteran who races from hold-up; W J Lee takes over and the horse wears a blindfold, returning after a 35-day break with modest sim-going figures (0W1P) and a recent second over course-and-distance at Goodwood suggesting he retains ability, but his deepest hold-up style is his biggest enemy in a race with a single uncontested front-runner.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time with a second after twice finishing sixth before that, The Highway Rat shows improvement without yet finding a win in five outings. He returns 35 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 7, sitting midfield on our figures.

runners_data.name: Howd'yadoit
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed pace-setter who won over this course-and-distance before on good ground; Colin Keane's booking is significant, and an 8-day turnaround for the Lyons yard (2/20 T14) is comfortable — however the STYLE_FIT tag (0.93) reminds that recent form shows some inconsistency when racing off a true front-running pitch, so he must translate lead advantage into a clean finish.
runners_data.comment: Won three starts back and has since raced creditably in fourth and seventh, Howd'yadoit returns just eight days after his latest outing. He has form over today's distance and going from draw 3, a leading contender on our figures despite not repeating that winning effort since.

runners_data.name: Eclairage
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up operator by nature whose best form (a 2nd at Goodwood GOO over 5f) came when closing late — wearing a tongue-tie here, and Daniel Murphy's yard has sent out no winner in 14 days (0/8); the redistribution to midfield on this map does not reflect how she will actually be ridden, and a true closing run over a flat 5f on Standard AW is a tough ask.
runners_data.comment: A midfield filly on our figures, Eclairage was runner-up four starts back. She has since tailed off, unplaced in two of her last three and winless throughout, and returns 14 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 1.

runners_data.name: Kerdos
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type who has finished in the frame at 6/1 over 5f on this surface before, but the form string (296860) reads poorly and the blindfold (b) is retained; Jack Kearney takes the 3lb claim which helps the weight, yet sim-going figures (0W1P) underline that converting hold-up runs into wins here is rare for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Best effort came when second six starts back, and Kerdos backs it up with a strong 89 speed figure despite six starts without a win. Unplaced last time, he returns 14 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 9.

runners_data.name: Ipanema Queen
runners_data.note: Three-year-old with a win and a place on this course over 5f on Standard, giving her genuine course-and-distance credentials; David Egan is a strong booking and De Aguiar has runners firing (same yard as Valiant Force), while a 23-day break looks fine — her prominent style suits a single front-runner scenario ideally and she is one of the few with a proven winning template here.
runners_data.comment: Our selection on overall profile, Ipanema Queen won five starts back, and was runner-up four starts back - form that underpins her case. She returns from a 23-day break with form over today's distance and going from draw 10, though a sixth last time is the one blot.

runners_data.name: Rosie Frith
runners_data.note: Dylan Browne McMonagle takes over on this filly who has won twice over 5f on Standard AW (once at Dundalk) and placed at 5f Standard going — her prominent, front-tracking style is perfectly calibrated for this race shape, and at only 10 days since last run she arrives fresh with in-running form that directly mirrors today's conditions.
runners_data.comment: Rosie Frith won last time out and has two wins from her last five starts, though an inconsistent middle spell (eighth, then unplaced) shows she can vary. Race-fit after just 10 days, she owns form over today's distance and going from draw 5.

runners_data.name: Collective Power
runners_data.note: Veteran eight-year-old who is naturally a prominent racer but is mapped to midfield here because this field cannot accommodate all the pace-pressing types — Chris Hayes rides, and the sim-going record (2W7P) over course and distance is genuinely strong; if he can find his preferred position he remains a threat, but his STYLE_FIT (0.92) flags the risk of racing out of his comfort zone.
runners_data.comment: Collective Power was runner-up two starts back but has otherwise struggled among six starts without a win, finishing ninth three runs ago. Fifth last time, he returns 35 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 8, sitting eighth of ten on our figures.

runners_data.name: Final Melody
runners_data.note: Consistent front-runner in her own right — five consecutive placed efforts at 5f including a Dundalk win and three seconds on Standard going — but she returns after a 212-day break which is a major flag, and Wayne Lordan has to manage a horse whose natural prominent instincts cannot be fully satisfied in this traffic-heavy pace scenario; the layoff makes it hard to trust her even if the style were perfectly placed.
runners_data.comment: Final Melody has been remarkably consistent, second in four of her last five starts and winning the other, but she hasn't run for 212 days, a lengthy absence that leaves her form stale. She has form over today's distance and going from draw 4.

runners_data.name: Fox In Flight
runners_data.note: Andrew Slattery rides this three-year-old whose best form is a 2nd over 5f on Good ground and a 3rd on Standard AW — a genuine prominent type who should naturally slot in just behind the leader; the Marnane yard is active (1/10 T14) and at 15 days since last run she is fit, though a career form of 3-8029 warns that placing ahead of more experienced rivals is not a given.
runners_data.comment: Fox In Flight was runner-up two starts back but that form has since unravelled with a ninth last time out, leaving him without a win in five starts. He returns 15 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 2.

races.paceDynamic: Howd'yadoit is the one confirmed front-runner in this 10-runner 5f handicap and, with no serious challenger for the lead, Colin Keane can control tempo from the front without being pressured into an unsustainable gallop — a sustainable, metronomic pace on Standard Dundalk AW is the likely outcome. Ipanema Queen, Rosie Frith, and Fox In Flight will push into prominent positions behind the leader, creating a compact early shape with genuine competition for the first two or three spots. The field is top-heavy with prominent-running types: Collective Power and Final Melody are natural prominent racers who cannot all get their preferred position, while Eclairage is a true hold-up horse pushed forward on the map — those displaced runners will find themselves racing out of their natural role. The tactical verdict favours horses who can sit handy just off a single uncontested front-runner at a controlled tempo and produce a sustained finish over 5f on AW — prominent types with course/distance form on Standard going are best positioned, with true deep closers facing a stiff ask if the pace is honest but not punishing.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Howd'yadoit Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Howd'yadoit is allowed a soft lead at a fair pace and prominent runners track smoothly without checking each other.
scenarios.body: Keane dictates a controlled but honest tempo and the prominent stalkers get a clean run to challenge inside the final furlong on the flat Dundalk track. Horses who can sit second or third and produce a strong sustained finish on Standard AW are the primary beneficiaries.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Leader Steals
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners fail to mount a coordinated challenge and Howd'yadoit is allowed to coast home on a slow-burning pace.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied, Keane extends the lead approaching the 2f pole and the hold-up horses are left with too much ground to make up on a sharp 5f track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Get Lucky Run
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is stronger than anticipated and the hold-up horses get a clear run through to challenge late.
scenarios.body: A contested first two furlongs would drain the leaders and give Valiant Force or The Highway Rat a rare opportunity to finish through on this course. Both face a fundamental challenge on a track that rarely suits deep hold-up horses over 5f, meaning this scenario depends on a pace misfiring that current evidence does not strongly support.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Causes Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the surplus of prominent types cause interference or checked runs early, scrambling the intended race shape.
scenarios.body: Collective Power and Final Melody, both natural prominent racers unable to slot into their preferred position, could create crowding that unbalances several runners. In that chaotic scenario a horse with wide draw or willingness to settle away from trouble picks up the pieces, but this outcome is low-probability given the experienced jockeys and straightforward 5f layout.

watchPoints.text: Rosie Frith and Ipanema Queen are both proven prominent types on Standard Dundalk 5f — if they settle cleanly behind Howd'yadoit, the first two home are most likely to come from this trio and any late drift in their market should be noted.

Final Melody has been off 212 days and, despite possessing the strongest recent form profile over this course and trip, an extended absence after a busy campaign makes her first-time fitness extremely uncertain — watch the betting for stable confidence signals.

Collective Power and Final Melody are natural prominent runners who cannot both secure their preferred position; if they bump or check each other in the first two furlongs, the horses immediately behind them — Fox In Flight or Rosie Frith — could inherit a clear run at the perfect moment.

Howd'yadoit's ability to hold a lead comfortably will define the entire race shape — if Keane is taken on early by any prominent runner drifting forward, the pace will lift and the hold-up horses such as Valiant Force gain a small but meaningful upgrade in their scenario probability.

Eclairage, mapped to midfield but a genuine hold-up type, will be ridden for a late run she is unlikely to get on an uncontested 5f pace — monitor her race position early as a proxy for whether the field has compressed or spread, which signals whether the closers have any realistic chance.

races.name: RACING TV FREE ONE MONTH TRIAL Handicap

runners_data.name: Reimagined
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly who fades in finishes on turf; recent form is poor with several double-figure finishes, trainer at 1/9 over 14 days, and a step up to 7f here may not solve the tendency to drop away late.
runners_data.comment: Reimagined tops our figures on a strong 74 speed figure, with a third two starts back showing she retains ability despite being yet to win in five starts. Only ninth last time out, she returns 11 days on with form over today's distance as the one to beat on figures.

runners_data.name: Wild Berries
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type with a habit of fading in the finish; 39 days off, trainer has a poor 14-day strike rate of 0/10, and while the 7f trip is not unfamiliar, she has struggled to get competitive in similar company.
runners_data.comment: Wild Berries ranks among the leading dangers on our figures despite modest recent form, unplaced last time out and without a win in five starts. She has form over today's distance from draw 6, but a 39-day absence leaves her fitness the obvious question.

runners_data.name: Iff In Doubt
runners_data.note: Genuine closer with a win at this trip and course (1/7f/STA) and a placed effort over 8f here; the overcrowded hold-up group forces her out of her natural rear position, which directly compromises her ability to produce the late run her style demands — style fit is reduced accordingly.
runners_data.comment: Iff In Doubt won three starts back, then was runner-up two starts back - form that reads well before a fifth last time out. He returns after a lengthy 69-day absence, with form over today's distance and going from draw 8, a fair midfield player on our figures.

runners_data.name: Kc Bear
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with solid placed form at Dundalk over both 6f and 8f, including a course win; Colin Keane retains the ride, trainer T14 at 2/12 is reasonable, and sitting just off the pace in a race with only one natural front-runner is a natural fit for this horse.
runners_data.comment: Kc Bear has been admirably consistent, winning four starts back and never finishing worse than fourth in five starts, with a second last time out. He returns 11 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 10, though his 53 speed figure is modest.

runners_data.name: Gonna Be Golden
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner with a Dundalk 7f win on standard going in its form; the STYLE_FIT flag reflects it is technically classified as prominent rather than pure lead, but in this field it will effectively set the fractions — controlled front-running is its clearest route to winning.
runners_data.comment: Gonna Be Golden has strung together mixed form, including an unseat and two unplaced efforts, but rallied to third last time out and can point to a win in her last five starts. She returns 23 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 5.

runners_data.name: Sagasti
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with Dundalk placed form (3/7f/STA) though only 2 runs from 6 on similar going show varying form; visor fitted, 11 days since last run, and the strong jockey booking of Dylan Browne McMonagle is the main interest — needs pace and a clear run.
runners_data.comment: Sagasti ranks among the leading dangers on our figures, having twice finished third in her last five starts without a win. She was unplaced last time out, the main concern, but returns 11 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 3.

runners_data.name: Fate's Gambit
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer whose best efforts come from a positive position; no win from 6 starts but four top-five finishes including a placed effort at Dundalk over 7f, and trainer angle is thin at 0/4 over 14 days — reliable place contender rather than a winner.
runners_data.comment: Fate's Gambit boasts a strong 78 speed figure but remains without a win in six starts, including an unplaced run last time out. His best effort came when runner-up six starts back. He returns 30 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 7.

runners_data.name: Whistling Jamesie
runners_data.note: True hold-up horse with a tendency to fade, whose natural position at the back is unavailable given the congested closing group; the redistribution to midfield means it races against its instincts and the STYLE_FIT discount is material — course win at Dundalk on standard is the only real positive.
runners_data.comment: Whistling Jamesie won four starts back but has since faded, following an eighth with two unplaced efforts including last time out. He returns 39 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 1, with a 70 speed figure his main asset.

runners_data.name: Mountain Memory
runners_data.note: Unknown quantity with only three runs and an unconventional angle of trainer also listed as jockey Andrew Slattery; no going or trip form to lean on, though the trainer's 14-day rate of 3/28 suggests some activity — hard to assess and likely an outsider at best.
runners_data.comment: Lightly raced with just three recent starts, Mountain Memory has yet to threaten - unplaced last time out, eighth two starts back, fifth three starts back, all winless. He returns 15 days on with form over today's distance from draw 11, a 66 speed figure offering little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Bullet Bourbon
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 52; a natural closer pushed into midfield by the overcrowded hold-up group, and with only one placed run from 14 on similar going, the combination of low class, compromised position, and fading tendencies makes this a difficult winning proposition.
runners_data.comment: Bullet Bourbon was runner-up five starts back but has since failed to better sixth in four subsequent outings without a win. She returns 10 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 9, sitting second-bottom of the field on our figures.

runners_data.name: Push Harder
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse on a step down to 7f from habitual 8f trips, having never won from 7 starts; the redistribution to midfield due to the overloaded rear group means it races out of its natural role, and the low trainer 14-day strike rate of 0/3 provides no compensating angle.
runners_data.comment: Push Harder's best recent form came three starts back when third, but she has since drifted to sixth and seventh, still without a win in five starts. She returns 28 days on with form over today's distance and going from draw 2.

races.paceDynamic: Gonna Be Golden is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no serious challenger for the lead, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front on standard Dundalk going. The hold-up contingent is heavily overloaded — Iff In Doubt, Whistling Jamesie, Bullet Bourbon, and Push Harder are all genuine closers but there are too many for the map to accommodate at the rear, meaning several will be forced to race closer to the pace than their natural style demands and are unlikely to produce their best from that compromised position. Kc Bear and Fate's Gambit are the natural prominent types best placed to sit just off Gonna Be Golden's shoulder and apply pressure at the right moment, while Sagasti, Reimagined, and Wild Berries will need a strong pace to generate any late momentum. A steady, front-runner-dictated race on a flat all-weather surface with an overloaded hold-up group strongly favours horses racing prominently who can quicken off a controlled pace, as the true closers are either compromised in position or face an insufficient pace injection to reel in a well-in-front rival.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gonna Be Golden Dictates
scenarios.trigger: If Gonna Be Golden settles comfortably in front and no rival applies sustained pressure, setting a measured pace throughout.
scenarios.body: Gonna Be Golden controls the race from the front and, on a flat standard surface with no challenger, simply quickens clear in the final two furlongs before hold-up horses can close; its Dundalk winning form and trainer angle give it strong claims from this position.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Kc Bear or Fate's Gambit travels strongly just off the pace and the gallop quickens early enough to expose hold-up horses.
scenarios.body: A positive-ridden horse sits a length or two off Gonna Be Golden and hits the front two furlongs out before closers can organise their challenges; Colin Keane's course craft on Kc Bear makes this profile particularly relevant given the horse's placed record at this track.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves stronger than expected and genuine closers Iff In Doubt or Sagasti find clear runs to produce sustained late finishes.
scenarios.body: A fast early tempo stretches the field and creates enough space for a true hold-up runner to pick off rivals in the closing stages, though the redistribution of so many closers to mid-division means their position is compromised from the outset.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles Form
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding, a false pace, or a slowdown mid-race scrambles positions and allows an unfancied runner to benefit from a fluky tactical setup.
scenarios.body: Mountain Memory or Wild Berries, both showing unknown or inconsistent form, could capitalise if the race falls apart and pace judgement rather than raw ability decides the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Gonna Be Golden's early break — if Sam Coen (5) sends it to the front cleanly and no rival follows, the race could be effectively over by halfway as the hold-up horses have too much ground to make up from compromised positions.

Kc Bear's position in the first furlong — Colin Keane will likely look to sit a length off the leader, and if he settles smoothly, the horse's Dundalk placed form makes it the main danger to the front-runner turning for home.

Iff In Doubt's run from midfield — naturally a closer with course winning form, if W J Lee finds a clear passage from the two-furlong pole the horse could finish powerfully, but a clean run is far from guaranteed in a field where it cannot reach its natural position.

Sagasti's headgear — the visor is a significant flag and Dylan Browne McMonagle's booking lifts this runner's profile considerably; if the visor sharpens early focus and the horse settles, it has the best jockey in the race and Dundalk placed form to be involved.

The overall pace volume — there are more front-running and prominent types in this field than can all get their desired position; Whistling Jamesie, Iff In Doubt, Bullet Bourbon, and Push Harder will all be forced to race closer than ideal, and how they handle that compression in the first two furlongs will shape whether any of them can still produce a credible finish.

races.name: Anglo Printers - Award Winning Print And Packaging Maiden
QuinnBet Handicap (0-60)

runners_data.name: Kitty Bear
runners_data.note: The race architect — won over course and distance in similar conditions and is handed a golden opportunity to dictate from the front completely unchallenged; Orla Tynan's 7lb claim is a meaningful weight relief; the pace scenario is tailor-made.
runners_data.comment: Kitty Bear has two wins in her last six starts and a strong 70 speed figure, backed by a rating of 65 with us. She was only 8th last time out, but the win form gives her real claims. Fit at 9 days with today's distance and going covered, she races from draw 17.

runners_data.name: Navajo Point
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator whose fade flag is a significant concern in a race likely to be run at a steady tempo; Dundalk form is absent and this Haydock-type profile looks misaligned with what today's race shape will demand.
runners_data.comment: Navajo Point boasts an eye-catching 79 speed figure and sits second in our order on 66 despite being winless in his last four starts. He does have today's distance proven and breaks from stall 1, though a below-par 8th last time out is the concern.

runners_data.name: Famous Enough
runners_data.note: Tongue-tie fitted, prominent racer with a decent course and distance second (2/8f/STA) in recent history; Patrick Foley's yard is not in a hot streak but this horse's natural position means it should be on or near the pace from the off.
runners_data.comment: Famous Enough was only 5th last time out and has been unplaced more than once in his last five starts, though a 2nd does stand out. He does have today's distance and going covered, fit at 11 days, but a modest 53 rating, 13th of 17, tells its own story.

runners_data.name: Micasso
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse in reality — recent Dundalk win (1/8f/GOO) shows ability, but the redistribution into midfield reflects that the field is stacked with closers; a steady pace will make it very hard to replicate that win from further back than ideal.
runners_data.comment: Micasso won last time out and has a 2nd in his last five starts too, showing he retains real ability, yet he sits down in 15th of 17 on our figures at 52. He arrives fit at 10 days with today's distance and going form in the book, from draw 12.

runners_data.name: Akashaa
runners_data.note: Chris Hayes partners a horse whose natural inclination is to race deep, but this Standard Dundalk surface (2/8f/STA runner-up) does indicate it handles conditions — the tactical squeeze in a field this large risks compromising its finish entirely.
runners_data.comment: Akashaa is winless in her last five starts, without ever finishing worse than 8th, and a 2nd in that sequence hints at ability. Back after 24 days off, she does have today's distance and going covered, rates a modest 54, and runs from draw 13.

runners_data.name: Movin And Groovin
runners_data.note: Absent 429 days and that layoff demands a large leap of faith; prominent style is a positive fit for today's race shape but the fitness question from that lengthy break is enormous.
runners_data.comment: Movin And Groovin is winless in her last five starts, though two 3rd-place efforts show she stays competitive, and she rates a workmanlike 57 with us. The concern is a lengthy absence — 429 days since her last run — despite today's distance and going form being in the book from draw 10.

runners_data.name: Bella Colombia
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR=60 and a natural hold-up type trained by Willie McCreery with a Dundalk win (1/8f/STA) in recent form — the class edge here is real and WJ Lee is a significant jockey booking; best placed of the closers to defy the pace shape.
runners_data.comment: Bella Colombia was runner-up last time out and has a win among her last six starts, with today's distance and going form already in the book. Fit again at 11 days and rated 66 with us — top of the field — though a testing 142 lb from draw 15 is the concern.

runners_data.name: Captain Ciano
runners_data.note: Fade flag in combination with poor recent form (500098) and a distance record skewed toward 10f+ makes this 8f Dundalk mile look unlikely to suit; trainer McCourt sends it back quickly but the data is unpromising.
runners_data.comment: Captain Ciano has today's distance and going form in the book and returns quickly, just 10 days after his latest run. Winless in his last six starts, he still rates 65 with us — good enough to feature — though a modest 59 speed figure is a slight query.

runners_data.name: Angel Of Promise
runners_data.note: Fades in finishes and has been campaigning mainly over 6-7f on good ground — stepping up to a mile at Dundalk under Ed Lynam, whose yard has one win from four in 14 days, looks speculative; headgear change (visor) noted.
runners_data.comment: Angel Of Promise is winless in her last five starts, with three unplaced efforts and a 9th among them, and returns after a 39-day absence. She does have today's distance form in her favour, but the layoff and modest recent figures make her hard to trust fully.

runners_data.name: Rockbury Lad
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a fade flag and a string of mid-pack finishes on the relevant going (4/15 similar-going runs, no wins); Colin Keane is elite but even that booking cannot mask that this horse repeatedly fails to sustain its effort.
runners_data.comment: Rockbury Lad is winless in his last six starts, but a 3rd among them shows he retains some ability, and he was seventh last time out. Fit again at 9 days, with today's distance and going form banked, he rates a workmanlike 61 — competitive without standing out.

runners_data.name: Fleetfootsoldier
runners_data.note: Prominent-racing profile is a tactical positive and the Dundalk surface form is there (2/7f/STA runner-up); two wins from 15 similar-going runs shows it does fire on this surface, though recent form figures (29-890) suggest a frustrating horse.
runners_data.comment: Fleetfootsoldier has struggled for placings recently, unplaced last time out after a run of finishes no higher than 8th, albeit a 2nd stands out further back in his form. Back after 24 days off, he has today's distance and going covered, though a modest 57 rating leaves plenty to find.

runners_data.name: Rampage
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up type displaced into a midfield slot; recent form (086700) is simply too poor to invite confidence even if the pace were to collapse, and McCourt's second runner in the race adds a complication.
runners_data.comment: Rampage is winless in his last six starts and has managed no better than 6th in that spell, but a strong 71 speed figure underpins a rating of 62 with us, sixth in the field. Fit at 10 days with today's distance and going covered, he races from draw 16.

runners_data.name: My Vonnie
runners_data.note: Clearly prefers longer trips — historical form is almost entirely over 10-12f; bumped down to a mile here and shown here in a midfield slot because of redistribution, this looks the wrong trip on every metric.
runners_data.comment: My Vonnie is winless in her last five starts, with finishes no better than 6th, and sits 14th of 17 on a modest 52 rating. She does have today's distance and going form and a fair 66 speed figure, but a 128-day layoff is a concern; she races from draw 11.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Force
runners_data.note: The most Dundalk-familiar horse in the field with 11 of 15 similar-going runs on this very surface; form figures (-66357) are modest but the recent third (3/7f/STA) shows it is competitive — true hold-up type that will need something to go wrong up front.
runners_data.comment: Cosmic Force is winless in his last five starts, but a 3rd in that sequence and a solid 68 speed figure support a rating of 55 with us. He was only 7th last time out and is back after 47 days off, though today's distance and going are proven from draw 2.

runners_data.name: Monroe Dasher
runners_data.note: No jockey listed and a Slipped/Unseated in recent form (000S-0); a fade flag plus zero wins from hold-up positions in this field makes this one of the harder cases to argue for regardless of scenario.
runners_data.comment: Monroe Dasher has struggled badly in recent starts, never placing and even slipping up once, and sits bottom of our figures at 38, 17th of 17. He does have today's distance covered and returns 23 days after his latest run, from draw 14, but there's little on offer here.

runners_data.name: Roman Harry
runners_data.note: Sammy Duffy's yard has one winner from two in 14 days and the horse has placed form on Standard going; genuine hold-up type placed in midfield by redistribution — the best-case scenario requires pace to lift and a clear passage that may not materialise.
runners_data.comment: Roman Harry is winless in his last six starts but has been competitive, with a 3rd and a pair of 4ths among his recent form, and a strong 71 speed figure supports our 62 rating. He was only 9th last time out, fit again at 10 days with today's distance and going covered, from draw 5.

runners_data.name: Desert Of The Sea
runners_data.note: Three placings from six Standard-going runs (0W3P) show honest consistency but no winning punch; the McCourt third runner in this race, a true rear-of-field horse shifted into midfield, is highly unlikely to manufacture a winning move from this position.
runners_data.comment: Desert Of The Sea has two seconds and a third among his last six starts and a promising 70 speed figure, yet sits second-bottom of our figures at 42. He was unplaced last time out and remains without a win, though fit at 10 days with today's distance and going covered, from draw 6.

races.paceDynamic: Kitty Bear is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 17-strong field and, critically, faces no genuine pace pressure — she can stride to the front from her prominent position and control tempo entirely on her own terms at Dundalk's flat, galloping mile. With Famous Enough and Fleetfootsoldier as the only other confirmed prominent types, the early sections will be orderly rather than frantic, producing a sustainable pace that will not burn off the front-runner. The bulk of this field — Bella Colombia, Captain Ciano, Angel Of Promise, Rockbury Lad, Navajo Point and several redistributed hold-up types — will queue behind and wait for a finish that may never truly materialise if Kitty Bear rolls along unchallenged. This race shape heavily favours the prominent-racing profile: a horse who can sit just off the pace in second or third and produce a decisive kick before the field can organise, rather than a true closer who must reel in a controlled gallop from deep. Several runners tagged as redistributed — including Micasso, Roman Harry, Akashaa and Desert Of The Sea — are genuine hold-up types who are unlikely to secure their natural position or find the late surge they need against an uncontested leader.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kitty Bear Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Kitty Bear leads from the outset, dictates a sustainable tempo and the large hold-up contingent fails to mount a coordinated challenge.
scenarios.body: Kitty Bear sets a metronomic gallop on the front end with no rival willing or able to pressurise, and the race simply never gets away from her before the straight; the early positions within striking distance are premium real estate.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or just-off-the-pace runner tracks Kitty Bear closely through the race and produces a sharp, well-timed move entering the straight.
scenarios.body: Bella Colombia or Famous Enough, sitting a length or two off the leader, exploits their superior class or fitness to collar Kitty Bear before the hold-up brigade can reach them; a prompt pace makes it very hard for anything coming from further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Rush Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Kitty Bear ties up in the final furlong, allowing a strong finisher to mow her down in the closing stages.
scenarios.body: Bella Colombia or Akashaa, travelling well through the division, finds a run down the rail in the straight and catches a weakening leader; this scenario is structurally less likely given the true hold-up types are redistributed and may not find their rhythm.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the large field results in scrimmaging and an unusually fast or erratic early tempo that burns off the leader prematurely.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a sprint finish from the final two furlongs with several runners in contention simultaneously; redistributed midfield types who handle a stronger pace and possess finishing speed could steal into contention, though most lack the profile to benefit.

watchPoints.text: Kitty Bear faces zero confirmed pace rivals — watch whether Famous Enough or Fleetfootsoldier send early to test her, because if neither does, the race is effectively over by halfway.

Bella Colombia is the highest-rated hold-up type with an elite jockey booking (WJ Lee) and genuine course-winning form — if she can travel smoothly in the first four, she represents the main danger to the front runner.

The redistributed hold-up contingent (Micasso, Roman Harry, Akashaa, Desert Of The Sea, Rampage) are all genuine closers who will be competing for the same ground down the back and into the straight — traffic congestion is a real risk for all of them.

Movin And Groovin's 429-day absence makes its early sectionals crucial — if it fails to stride forward naturally from stall to stall, it will compound the pace map by adding dead weight in the rear group rather than applying any pressure on Kitty Bear.
Monroe Dasher has no jockey confirmed — a final-declarations watch is warranted, and if it does run, the form figures and fade flag suggest it is a non-factor in any scenario.

races.name: Fairways Hotel Dundalk Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Celtic Druid
runners_data.note: Back-to-back Dundalk wins over 12f on Standard, now stepping to 14f where he is unexposed; sole genuine front-runner with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 suggesting this is technically out of his comfort zone but his track record here overrides that concern substantially.
runners_data.comment: Celtic Druid's two wins are further back in his form, with three subsequent efforts yielding nothing better than a 3rd, leaving him only 10th of 13 on our figures at 63. He does have today's distance and going covered and a strong 74 speed figure, and is fit again at 16 days, but the recent dip is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Dancing Steve
runners_data.note: Consistent back-marker who has struggled to convert promising positions, with a string of double-figure finishes on turf at Dundalk; headgear visor fitted, apprentice Sam Coen claims 2lb, but sim-going record of 0W4P offers little encouragement.
runners_data.comment: Dancing Steve is winless in his last five starts and has struggled for placings, with only a 6th to show in that spell. He does have today's distance and going covered and returns at 18 days, with a smart 79 speed figure supporting a strong 72 rating, fourth in the field.

runners_data.name: Baila Conmigo
runners_data.note: Won over 10f at Dundalk on Standard and ran well for second over 9f on Soft — a genuine hold-up horse whose natural closing run will be compromised here because the number of rear-dwellers means he is pushed into a midfield slot he would not choose.
runners_data.comment: Baila Conmigo has a win in his last six starts along with a 2nd and a 3rd, showing he's capable at this level, and rates 69 with us, fifth in the field. He was only 5th last time out and is back after 42 days off, though today's distance and going form is proven.

runners_data.name: Rich Belief
runners_data.note: Veteran of nine seasons, most effective at extreme distances — his best recent form includes a win over 17f and a place at 18f on Good; the drop to 14f and 78-day absence (33 days with this jockey) are concerns, tongue-tie fitted.
runners_data.comment: Rich Belief has a 2nd among his last five starts and a strong 70 speed figure, marking him out as a leading contender at 73 on our figures, third in the field. He was only unplaced last time out and is without a win in that sequence, though today's distance and going form is banked.

runners_data.name: Porsche Lad
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer with two wins over 7f on Standard at Dundalk and a recent third over 12f here; blinkers applied, and at 9 days since last run he arrives in good order — the key pace threat to Celtic Druid.
runners_data.comment: Porsche Lad has been knocking on the door, with two 2nds and a 3rd among his last six starts, and rates a strong 77 with us. He's quickly back in action after just 9 days and has today's distance and going form proven, with only a lack of a win in that spell to hold against him.

runners_data.name: Tero D'rosa
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on Good and placed over 10f on Standard; stepping up to 14f for the first time and trainer Ross O'Sullivan in excellent 4/20 form over 14 days — the trip is the question mark but the form profile is solid.
runners_data.comment: Tero d'Rosa has a win in his last five starts plus a 2nd and a 3rd, showing solid recent form, and rates 64 with us, ninth in the field. He was 6th last time out and is back at 30 days, with today's going already proven, though a modest 62 speed figure is a mild concern.

runners_data.name: Chopsticks
runners_data.note: Front-runner flag on the form card with a hood fitted; placed in a 12f Standard race at Dundalk but has struggled over extreme distances; trainer McConnell quiet at 0/22 over 14 days — needs to find a prominent position quickly with several rivals wanting the same ground.
runners_data.comment: Chopsticks has a win in his last five starts along with a 2nd, 3rd and 4th, showing solid form figures, and rates 69 with us, sixth in the field. Fit at 30 days with today's distance and going covered, the concern is the trainer's recent form — no winner from 22 runners in the last fortnight.

runners_data.name: Rising Sky
runners_data.note: Has shown only one win from 15 attempts on Standard in sim-going and that came at shorter; tongue-tie and cheekpieces worn, quick 9-day turnaround, but his Dundalk form over 12f was a distant 11th last time.
runners_data.comment: Rising Sky has a win among her last six starts plus a 3rd, though results have been mixed, including an 8th and a 7th, and she was only unplaced last time out. Quickly back at 9 days with today's distance and going covered, she rates 66 with us, eighth in the field.

runners_data.name: Grey Fable
runners_data.note: Won over 12f at Dundalk on Standard but that was two runs back — a genuine closer whose preference for coming from behind is noted, yet the redistribution here means he will sit in midfield rather than his true late-running position; tongue fitted.
runners_data.comment: Grey Fable has a win in his last five starts plus a 4th, but was only 9th last time out having also been unplaced in that spell. Back at 22 days with today's distance and going covered, a solid 68 speed figure supports his 67 rating, seventh in the field.

runners_data.name: Sutton Hoo
runners_data.note: Top weight at OR 71 and a winner over 10f at Dundalk on Standard, racing fresh at 44 days; only four career runs means he is lightly raced and unexposed at this trip — genuine class edge if he can find a clear late run.
runners_data.comment: Sutton Hoo has a win among his last four starts, with the others including an unplaced effort, a 9th and a 6th, yet he tops our figures at 77. Back after a 44-day break with today's going covered, he heads this field on pure form but the layoff is a query.

runners_data.name: Sonny Corleone
runners_data.note: Young Gordon Elliott three-year-old with only three career runs; placed twice on Standard over 10f but steps up significantly in trip here — trainer in strong 5/46 form over 14 days is the main angle, but limited experience at 14f is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Sonny Corleone is winless in his last three starts, with two 4ths and an unplaced effort among them, and rates only 62 with us, 11th in the field. He does have today's going covered and a fair 66 speed figure, but a 44-day break adds to the task.

runners_data.name: Mystic Rose
runners_data.note: Lowest OR in the field at 50; recent form string of 640755 offers no basis for optimism — a true hold-up horse who, with the field stacked at the rear, ends up mapped to midfield in a spot that suits her even less; tongue and pads fitted.
runners_data.comment: Mystic Rose is winless in her last six starts and has never finished better than 4th in that spell. She sits 12th of 13 on our figures at 57 but does have today's distance covered and a fair 69 speed figure, fit again at 10 days.

runners_data.name: Folk Warrior
runners_data.note: Placed twice over 12f and 10f on Standard and Soft, but a 22-day absence for a trainer with no recent runners (T14:0/0) raises questions about readiness; another natural closer pushed into a midfield role by the weight of hold-up types in this field.
runners_data.comment: Folk Warrior is winless in his last four starts, with finishes no better than 4th and a pair of unplaced efforts, and sits bottom of our figures at 55. He does have today's distance and going covered and a fair 69 speed figure, back at 22 days, but he's up against it here.

races.paceDynamic: Celtic Druid is the sole confirmed front-runner in a 13-runner field and, carrying the form of back-to-back Dundalk wins at this track, will stride to the front and set a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 1m4f trip on Standard going. Behind him, Porsche Lad, Tero D'rosa, Chopsticks, and Rising Sky will all push for prominent positions, creating a competitive early jostle for the handful of seats just off the leader. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate cleanly at the rear — Baila Conmigo, Grey Fable, Mystic Rose, and Folk Warrior are true closers who are likely to find themselves further forward than ideal, with only Sutton Hoo, Dancing Steve, and Sonny Corleone likely to secure genuine hold-up berths. With one uncontested, confident pace-setter and a contested midfield scramble behind, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently in the slipstream of Celtic Druid — patient prominent runners who can track the leader and produce a clean, well-timed challenge in the straight will be best served by this setup.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Celtic Druid Controls Gallop
scenarios.trigger: If Celtic Druid is allowed to dictate a modest, uncontested tempo and kicks clear from the home turn.
scenarios.body: Celtic Druid's two back-to-back wins at Dundalk over 12f show he handles this track and loves Standard going, and at 14f he can simply extend his lead unchallenged while rivals bottled up in the midfield scramble are left with too much to do.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely sustainable and a prominent tracker produces a well-timed challenge inside the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A horse sitting second or third, saving ground through the bend and striking as Celtic Druid begins to tie up, would benefit most from the clean run this shape allows.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Finds Gap Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to stop the race at the top of the straight and create a genuine run-in for closers.
scenarios.body: Sutton Hoo arrives fresh to this trip with the highest OR in the field and one Dundalk win already to his name, giving him the class edge if a true run materialises late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Benefits Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent runners set a strong early tempo that burns out and a midfield mover sweeps through beaten horses.
scenarios.body: This is a low-probability shape given Celtic Druid's proven tendency to dictate calmly rather than blaze, but a horse like Baila Conmigo, who has shown finishing ability at Dundalk, could be the beneficiary if the race falls apart.

watchPoints.text: Celtic Druid is uncontested on the front end and his two recent Dundalk wins make him the immediate danger if Sadhbh Tormey settles him smoothly and he travels without cover — watch whether any of the prominent quartet (Porsche Lad, Tero D'rosa, Chopsticks, Rising Sky) pushes up to challenge him in the opening half-mile.

Porsche Lad and Chopsticks both carry front-running tendencies and both want the same prominent real estate — watch the early exchanges for a contested lead developing that could compromise both their chances.

Sutton Hoo carries the highest OR at 71 and is a Dundalk winner on Standard; watch whether Paddy Harnett positions him just off the midfield scramble to produce a clean run in the straight rather than getting buried in traffic.

Several hold-up horses (Baila Conmigo, Grey Fable, Mystic Rose, Folk Warrior) are genuine closers forced forward by the race shape — if any of them drift back to their natural position at the rear, monitor whether the pace-setter has built enough of a cushion to hold them off.

Tero D'rosa's trainer Ross O'Sullivan is in strong form at 4/20 over 14 days — watch if the market reflects stable confidence on this first attempt at 14f, as a well-backed move here would be significant given the form step up in trip.

races.name: Border Boutique Hire Maiden

runners_data.name: Dorie Miller
runners_data.note: Lightly exposed veteran hold-up horse who has repeatedly faded in the finish at distances up to 19f on better ground — the controlled pace this shape creates will not generate the late sectionals needed to showcase any staying power, and a 36-day break adds uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Let's Smash It
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, returning after a 219-day absence for a trainer in 1/6 form over 14 days — its sole start produced a second over 8f on standard going, which is relevant, but the long layoff is the primary concern; style-fit flag confirms it is racing somewhat out of usual role at this prominent extreme.

runners_data.name: Matties Point
runners_data.note: Lightly raced three-year-old with unknown going preference and no accessible form string — W J Lee is a high-class booking that hints at ability, and the clean slate makes this horse impossible to dismiss or strongly support; everything hinges on unexposed talent.

runners_data.name: Police Gazette
runners_data.note: Has two runs on standard Dundalk going, finishing third over this exact 12f trip most recently, which is directly relevant form — hold-up style means the steady tempo that Let's Smash It will create works against a horse that needs the race to develop strongly; Gavin Ryan will need to be creative with positioning.

runners_data.name: Reynir
runners_data.note: Consistent prominent racer for JP Murtagh's yard who has placed twice over 10f on good ground — stepping up to 10.5f here on a flat, standard surface with Ben Coen aboard should suit, and his natural front-tracking style puts him in the ideal position if Let's Smash It controls proceedings.

runners_data.name: Perggosa
runners_data.note: A true hold-up horse by nature — rated just 42 and carrying a fade-in-finish flag after a run of double-digit finishes — the midfield map position reflects redistribution rather than a change in running style, and Cleary will ride from off the pace; very hard to see a route to victory with this profile in a steady-tempo race.

races.paceDynamic: Let's Smash It is the sole confirmed front-runner in this six-runner maiden over 1m2½f at Dundalk and will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop from the outset, dictating terms without any meaningful pressure from rivals. Reynir is the other prominent type and will look to track Let's Smash It closely, creating a two-horse lead group ahead of a midfield cluster. Perggosa is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed to midfield on the map because the rear is lighter than the field's true composition — Cleary will be ridden from off the pace regardless of where the map places them. Dorie Miller and Police Gazette are the natural closers, though with only one true front-runner setting a controlled tempo, the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can travel comfortably in the first two or three, as a sedate gallop is unlikely to set up a meaningful late run from behind.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Smash It dictates a steady, uncontested tempo and the race resolves into a sustained gallop home from the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: Let's Smash It sets the fractions exactly as it pleases, and Reynir, travelling prominently throughout, is best placed to challenge when the pace lifts in the straight. A controlled pace over this distance on standard Dundalk AW heavily favours horses racing in the first three who do not need to make ground from behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Fades, Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Let's Smash It or Reynir overcooks the pace or weakens sharply in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: A fractionally stronger gallop than expected would leave the leaders vulnerable inside the final furlong, giving the hold-up runners a chance to close. Police Gazette, with proven standard-going form over the trip, is the most credible beneficiary from the back of the field if the pace collapses.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Unexposed Type Lands It
scenarios.trigger: If Matties Point, the lightly raced unknown quantity, proves significantly better than the bare form of the field suggests.
scenarios.body: With style listed as unknown and minimal form exposed, Matties Point is the wildcard — if W J Lee slots into a handy position and the horse proves a natural on this surface, its freshness could be telling in a steady-run maiden. This scenario hinges on raw ability outweighing tactical positioning, making it a lower-probability but non-trivial outcome.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the pace somehow collapses entirely and a strong late surge materialises from the rear.
scenarios.body: Perggosa and Dorie Miller are the natural hold-up horses, but both carry fade-in-finish warnings and Perggosa is a redistribution case — their true closing style is compromised by limited ability to sustain a run. A sustained late sweep from these two requires a genuinely strong pace that this sole front-runner race shape is unlikely to generate.

watchPoints.text: Reynir must be monitored as the most prominent threat to Let's Smash It — if Ben Coen positions him directly behind the leader from the off, he becomes the horse best-placed to benefit from the controlled pace shape and could prove the one to beat.

Let's Smash It's 219-day absence is significant for a two-year-old returning for a different yard — if it shows signs of ring-rustiness early or is unable to sustain the gallop, the entire pace dynamic collapses and the scenarios restructure around who can pick up the pieces.

Matties Point is a complete unknown — watch the market before post time; if W J Lee's booking translates into serious market support for a horse with no visible form, it should be treated as a live runner regardless of the style uncertainty.

Dorie Miller and Perggosa both carry fade-in-finish tags — if either is seen making unexpected headway at the two-furlong pole, it may signal that the pace has been stronger than anticipated and late closers could be more competitive than the scenario probabilities suggest.

races.name: Family Funday At Dundalk Saturday 15th August Fillies Maiden

runners_data.name: Annacroft
runners_data.note: Highest official rating in the field at OR=120 but a 9-day turnaround after running over 8f at Good; a hold-up operator with a noted tendency to fade late, which is a meaningful concern if the pace is slow and she is asked to make up ground from the rear over this 1m2½f trip.

runners_data.name: Duvessa
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien sends out this four-year-old 22 days fresh with Dylan Browne McMonagle booked, the strongest jockey-trainer combination on the card; she is naturally prominent and carries a 0.90 style-fit flag, meaning her best form comes when able to dictate — here she almost certainly gets that role unopposed.

runners_data.name: Forthill
runners_data.note: 92 days off the track for Paul Twomey is the headline concern; showed placed form over 11-12f on Soft ground, so the Standard AW surface and the step back up to 1m2½f are not issues, and her prominent style makes her the most natural horse to track Duvessa if she arrives fit.

runners_data.name: Rocket Robyn
runners_data.note: Martin Hassett runner whose recent form figures of 9-8069 make bleak reading; a true hold-up horse by nature though the compressed six-runner field pushes her onto the map in midfield, and the 0.90 style-fit flag and headgear (t) suggest her chance depends heavily on conditions breaking her way.

runners_data.name: Tequila
runners_data.note: 290 days off the track — by far the longest absence in the field — for Robson De Aguiar; her similar-going record on Standard (2 runs, 0 wins, 0 places) adds another layer of doubt, and while she is mapped to midfield, she wants to close from the rear and her true hold-up style may leave her with too much to do.

runners_data.name: Wheres The Gold
runners_data.note: Paul Flynn's filly has been running consistently below par in the form figures (00/007) and her headgear (p) has not sparked improvement; she fades in finishes and is the shortest on last-run recency at eight days, but her class ceiling appears limited and she looks to be against it from a hold-up position on this evidence.

races.paceDynamic: Duvessa is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, she should coast into an uncontested, rhythm-controlled gallop from the front over this 1m2½f trip on Standard Dundalk AW. Forthill is the only other prominent-style runner and may attempt to track Duvessa, but with six runners and a modest pace the race is unlikely to develop into anything taxing early. Annacroft, Wheres The Gold, Tequila and Rocket Robyn are all hold-up types by nature, though Tequila and Rocket Robyn have been redistributed to midfield on the map because the field holds more hold-up horses than can realistically fill the rear slots — neither is likely to secure their natural position. The field being light on genuine pace and dominated by horses who want to close means the shape strongly favours a well-positioned prominent runner who controls the tempo and is not forced to burn energy early — Duvessa's ability to dictate an honest but unforced gallop is the defining tactical feature of this race.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Duvessa Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Duvessa is allowed to control a steady-to-fair tempo without serious early pressure from Forthill or any redistributed horse
scenarios.body: Duvessa leads at a metronomic gallop, keeps her rivals in a long single-file queue and has enough stamina reserve to repel late challengers over the 1m2½f trip; horses who sit in a comfortable tracking position directly behind her inherit the best ground and timing.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Tracker Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If Duvessa sets a strong-enough pace that a close tracker conserves energy and pounces in the final furlong
scenarios.body: A runner like Forthill or Annacroft sits just off the leader through the race, gets a clear run turning in and sustains a run that Duvessa cannot hold off in the dying strides; this benefits a horse with good tactical speed who can sit second or third early.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough and a genuine hold-up type finds a clear passage late to overhaul a tiring leader
scenarios.body: Annacroft or Wheres The Gold, sitting last or second-last, needs a clear enough run in a small six-runner field to close off a strong late burst; on a Standard surface over this trip the closing runs can land, but only if the pace genuinely tests the front two.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Bunches Field
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is so slow that the entire field converges turning in and it becomes a sprint from 2f out
scenarios.body: With six runners and a controlled gallop, the race could bunch dramatically in the straight, reducing the advantage of any specific running style and making the outcome dependent on raw finishing speed and position drawn; horses with a turn of foot and a clear early run benefit most.

watchPoints.text: Duvessa (Browne McMonagle) could dictate entirely on her own terms — watch whether Forthill attempts to press her early, because if Forthill challenges for the lead the pace increases and Duvessa's supremacy becomes less certain.

Forthill's 92-day absence is the biggest fitness unknown in the race — watch the parade ring closely for any signs of condition, as her involvement in the finish depends entirely on her returning to form first time back.

Tequila's 290-day layoff combined with a 0-from-2 record on Standard Dundalk AW makes her a significant risk — watch if she travels smoothly in the early stages, as any sign of struggling for rhythm would effectively rule her out.

With four genuine hold-up horses in a six-runner field, watch how the field fans out in the straight — if the pace is slow and they all close simultaneously, interference or a blocked run for Annacroft or Wheres The Gold is a real possibility.

Rocket Robyn wears a tongue-tie and has not finished in the first six in any of her last five runs — watch her early positioning to see whether she is ridden more prominently than her natural style, which would be the only scenario in which she becomes relevant late.
